identity.title: The Disk Substructures at High Angular Resolution Project (DSHARP). VI. Dust Trapping in Thin-ringed Protoplanetary Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: The data from the ALMA Large Programme DSHARP (cite: dsharp:andrews) offers an exciting new opportunity to put this concept to the test

question.value: Are the narrow high-contrast dust rings in DSHARP disks caused by dust trapping in radial pressure bumps, and what does this constrain about turbulence and grain size?

evidence.quote: In this paper we test the hypothesis that these dust rings are caused by dust trapping in radial pressure bumps, and if confirmed, put constraints on the physics of the dust trapping mechanism.
Planck function at $T_{\mathrm{d}}$ in band 6.

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: 1-D viscous disk evolution model with single dust species and Gaussian gap, applied to HD 163296 ring 2

evidence.quote: Our model is a 1-D viscous disk evolution model with a single dust component added, which can radially drift and will be prone to radial turbulent mixing.

method.value: MCMC fit of Gaussian A, r0, sigma to azimuthally averaged deprojected radial intensity profile in a by-eye radial domain

evidence.quote: We use the code emcee (cite: 2013PASP..125..306F) to perform a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) procedure to find the set of parameters $(A,r_0,\sigma)$ which have the highest likelihood.

key_parameters.value: 100 walkers, 500 steps, last 250 used; errors multiplied by sqrt(70)

evidence.quote: We use 100 walkers with 500 steps, and use the last 250 steps for our statistics.

assumptions.value: Gaussian ring shape; domain chosen by eye

evidence.quote: We choose by eye a radial domain around the bump where we believe a Gaussian description is justified.

evidence.quote: simulate the ALMA visibilities, put these data through the DSHARP imaging pipeline, and extract the radial profile.

analysis_steps.goal: Deconvolve beam and estimate temperature, scale height

method.value: w_d = sqrt(sigma^2 - sigma_b^2) with effective beam; T_d from irradiated flaring disk; h_p from T_d

evidence.quote: w_d=\sqrt{\sigma^2-\sigma_b^2}
We take the flaring angle to be $\varphi=0.02$ which is an estimate based on typical values from models.
Assuming that the gas temperature is equal to the dust temperature

method.value: tau_peak=-ln(1-A_dec/B_nu(T_d)); M_thin from Gaussian; optical depth correction via Gaussian mimicry factor

evidence.quote: \tau_\nu^{\mathrm{peak}} = -\ln\left(1-\frac{A_{\mathrm{dec}}}{B_{\nu}(T_d)}\right)

evidence.quote: yields a dust opacity of $\kappa_\nu^{\mathrm{abs}}(\lambda=0.125\,\mathrm{cm})=2.0{}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{g}$

analysis_steps.goal: Constrain trapping parameters (alpha/St, w, Sigma_g, grain size)

method.value: Analytic steady-state Gaussian trap model w_d=w(1+psi^-2)^-1/2; alpha/St=[(w/w_d)^2-1]^-1 for w_min and w_max; Toomre Q>2 upper limit on Sigma_g

evidence.quote: \frac{\alpha_{\mathrm{turb}}}{\mathrm{St}} \equiv \psi^{2} = \left[\left(\frac{w}{w_{\mathrm{d}}}\right)^2-1\right]^{-1}

evidence.quote: the average material density of the dust aggregates is $\xi_{\mathrm{dust}}\simeq 1.67{}\,\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}^3$

assumptions.value: Perfect trapping, fixed Gaussian pressure bump, no back-reaction

evidence.quote: The pressure bump is assumed to be so strong that the dust trapping in these rings is perfect: no dust escapes.

validation.value: Compared to 1-D numerical drift-diffusion model of a planet gap

evidence.quote: We see that the width of the numerical profile of the dust surface density is more or less consistent with the analytic result

evidence.loc: Computing dust mass including mild optical depth effects
evidence.quote: We use the ` scipy.optimize.minimize()` function of the SciPy library of Python
The rings have peak absorption optical depth in the range between 0.2 and 0.5.
we find that the strongest dust trapping occurs in AS 209, with $w_d/w$ ratios of 0.17 and 0.21 for rings 1 and 2, respectively.
All rings are radially resolved, by factors $\sigma/\sigma_b$ ranging from 1.6 (ring B41 of HD 143006) to 3.2 (ring B67 of HD 163296).
from opacity arguments we can put strong upper limits on the grain size of 1 cm to half a meter, depending on the ring.

findings_qualitative.value: Rings in AS 209, Elias 24, GW Lup and outer ring of HD 163296 are narrower than the estimated pressure scale height, evidence for dust trapping

evidence.quote: This is strong evidence for dust trapping being at work.

claims.hypothesis: The narrow DSHARP rings are caused by dust trapping in axisymmetric pressure bumps
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits to deprojected radial profiles, comparison of w_d to h_p and to the analytic trap model
claims.result: Several rings have w_d < h_p; all have w_d < w_max
claims.finding: All rings consistent with dust trapping; no evidence against it

evidence.quote: For none of the 8 rings studied in this paper we found evidence against dust trapping.

claims.experiment: Estimated tau_peak from deconvolved amplitude and Planck function with assumed T_d
claims.finding: Rings are moderately optically thick; dust masses are tens of Earth masses, opacity-limited

evidence.quote: The dust masses stored in each of these rings is of the order of tens of Earth masses

claims.hypothesis: Combination of very low turbulence and large grains is allowed
claims.experiment: Derived lower limit alpha_turb >= (a/0.02 cm) alpha_exmp
claims.finding: alpha << 5e-4 with a >> 0.1 cm is excluded

evidence.quote: the combination of very low $\alpha_{\mathrm{turb}}\ll 5\times 10^{-4}$ and very large grains $a_{\mathrm{grain}}\gg 0.1\,\mathrm{cm}$ can be excluded by the data

claims.hypothesis: Dust in rings may reach streaming instability conditions
claims.experiment: Volume density ratio criterion for AS 209 ring 1
claims.result: Triggered if Sigma_g <~ 1.4 g/cm^2, vs gravitational instability above 16

evidence.quote: The dust rings are dense enough to potentially trigger the streaming instability, but our analysis cannot give proof of this mechanism actually operating.

why_this_method.value: Image-plane fitting allows selecting individual rings independently of other emission

evidence.quote: because that allows us to select an individual ring, and study it independently of the emission elsewhere

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Grain size distribution as origin of wing excess: model is symmetric so cannot explain asymmetric excess

evidence.quote: However, the model is symmetric, so it cannot explain the asymmetric excess of most rings.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust opacity uncertain by a factor of 10; temperature only estimated

evidence.quote: can easily be wrong by a factor of $10$ upward or downward, with correspondingly large changes in the derived dust mass

limitations_admitted.value: Results not definitive; starting point for more complex modeling

evidence.quote: This paper is therefore not meant to give definitive numbers or conclusions.

referee_caveats_inferred: Midplane temperature relies on a fixed flaring angle of 0.02 for all disks
Gaussian domain chosen by eye; width differs 8-30% from uv-plane fits
Results depend strongly on opacity model and single grain size
Rings only 1.6-3 beams wide so deconvolution is delicate
